text:
Rajiv Patel: Quick follow-up on the MHA layout RFC — we didn't land a clear call on NHWC vs NCHW for the fused attention kernels. I'm worried about memory coalescing and padding effects for variable seq lengths. Thoughts?

Sara Kim: I lean NHWC (B, S, H, Dh) for clarity: contiguous head dims for TensorCores and easier `softmax` reduction across S. But NHWC can fragment Q/K/V if we interleave qkv.

Miguel Torres: +1 NHWC for tiled kernels. But two big caveats: 1) KV cache layout needs to be compatible — if our cache is [B, num_heads, S, Dh] and kernel expects NHWC, we need a cheap reinterpret or transpose. 2) For short sequences, NCHW-like packing (B, H*Dh, S) gives better L2 utilization.

Dina Chen: We measured this in the perf tests: for GPT-like shapes (B=1..8, S<=512, H=16..64, Dh=64) fused NHWC wins on throughput for long S because of coalesced head-dim loads. NCHW wins for tiny S (<=32) because it avoids the extra indexing math and gives densest CUDA memory accesses.

Rajiv Patel: Good data. What about contiguous QKV vs interleaved QKV? Implementation complexity vs memcpy costs?

Sara Kim: Interleaved QKV (QKV packed as [B, S, H, 3, Dh]) reduces separate GEMM passes but complicates kernel idx math. Contiguous (separate Q, K, V) needs 3x loads but simpler kernels and allows fused `q_proj` + `q_bias` in one pass.

Miguel Torres: We tried interleaved on Ampere and saw ~6-8% perf up for large B*S because it reduces L1 pressure — single read touches Q/K/V for a token. But it kills quantization-friendly layouts: int8 kernels like per-channel scales assume contiguous per-projection tensors.

Dina Chen: Also note cuBLAS/DEX kernels prefer NCHW-like contiguous row-major for batched GEMM. If we adopt NHWC + interleaved QKV, we need custom batched GEMM wrappers or staging buffers which adds memory traffic.

Rajiv Patel: So tradeoffs: NHWC + interleaved = best steady-state for large S, but more complex for KV cache and quantized kernels. NCHW + contiguous QKV = simpler, better for micro-batches / short S, and easier integration with cuBLAS.

Sara Kim: Another dimension: stride choices. If we choose NHWC, do we layout as [B, S, H, Dh] with Dh stride-1 (contiguous head inner) or [B, H, S, Dh] to favor head-major kernels? The first helps per-head TensorCore ops; the second helps scanning across sequence for streaming.

Miguel Torres: For streaming+kv-cache append, [B, H, S, Dh] is nice because appends are contiguous in S. But compute kernels then need gather by S which hurts coalescing. We benchmarked both: append-heavy workloads prefer head-major layout.

Dina Chen: Suggested compromise: primary in-memory cache uses [B, H, S, Dh] for cheap appends and network transfer; before compute, do a cheap 1-byte-per-element permutation into NHWC-like compute buffers when batch is large. The permute cost amortizes for S>64.

Rajiv Patel: That matches my intuition. Action items: 1) proto a small permute buffer + fused kernel path for NHWC compute (Miguel), 2) add microbench for quantized kernels with interleaved vs contiguous QKV (Dina), 3) update RFC with concrete layout recommendation and fallback (Sara).
